Subject: Trouble accepting supplier invite (NameID mismatch)

Hi Karthik / Ben,

We got the supplier invite for Opal Supplies but when I click the Accept link it fails during SSO with an error about the NameID not matching the expected attribute.

Steps I took:
- Clicked link from Chrome on Mac (latest)
- I get redirected to our IdP, authenticate, then land on an error page: "SAML assertion NameID does not match existing account"
- I attached a screenshot of the error and the invite link query string.

Can you tell us what attribute Redwood expects in NameID? Our IdP (Azure AD) sends userPrincipalName; some apps expect mail. We can change mapping but need to know what will work for the Coupa/Zip flow so we don't break other users.

We need this live before our first PO goes out on Monday — supplier needs to confirm banking/W-9. Is there a manual activation path if SSO can't be fixed quickly?

Thanks,
Marta Delgado
Procurement Operations
Opal Supplies

Attachments: opal-invite-screenshot.png
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trouble accepting supplier invite (NameID mismatch)

Hi Marta — thanks for the screenshot and the heads-up.

Short answer: Redwood's SP (for the supplier portal) prefers the NameID to be the user's primary email (mail attribute). If your Azure AD is sending userPrincipalName, that will usually work only when UPN == email. If your IdP mapping is currently sending a different identifier, that can cause the NameID mismatch on account rebind.

Immediate options:
1) Quick workaround: try the invite link in an incognito window or a different browser (sometimes existing SSO sessions cause attribute drift).
2) If that fails, Ben can generate a time-limited fallback accept link that tolerates NameID mismatch (we can enable a temporary parameter on the invite flow).
3) Manual activation: we can activate the supplier record on our side and send you a secure upload link for W-9/banking. This is what we normally do for urgent PO flows.

Ben — can you check the SAML logs for this invite and, if possible, produce a fallback accept link and the small saml-debug.txt that shows the assertion? Monica, adding you for operations so CS can follow up if we need manual activation or to record this in the onboarding checklist.

Marta — if you can share (a) the raw SAML response (if your IdP team can provide) or (b) confirm whether UPN == email in your tenant, that will help us decide whether to ask them to remap the NameID to mail.

I'll keep you posted.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 5, 2026 at 9:45 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben — can you check the SAML logs for this invite and, if possible, produce a fallback accept link and the small saml-debug.txt that shows the assertion?

Checked the logs for the invite token OPAL-INV-9882. The assertion we received had NameID=userPrincipalName (marta@opal.local) which doesn't match the existing supplier record (marta@opal-supplies.com). Two options:

- Recommended permanent fix: have the IdP send the mail claim as NameID (or set NameIDFormat to emailAddress and map to user.mail). That's the least disruptive.
- Short-term workaround: I created a temporary accept URL that accepts the invite by email address regardless of NameID: https://suppliers.redwood.ai/accept?token=OPAL-INV-9882&fallback=nameid
  - This link is single-use and expires in 48 hours.
  - I also attached saml-debug.txt with the minimal assertion fields (redacted) so your IdP team can see the mismatch.

Manual activation: if you prefer, we can manually create the Opal supplier record and send a secure upload link for W-9/bank docs. I attached the manual-activation-form.pdf and will process the activation as soon as you confirm. Manual activation also triggers a verification step to tie the supplier to your account before PO visibility is granted.

Let me know which route you want. If you want me to open a short support ticket for the IdP mapping change, I can do that and copy a staff engineer.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — the fallback link worked. I accepted the invite and completed the profile.

Two quick asks before we close the loop:
1) Can you confirm that when we publish the first PO from Opal (PO-7341) our finance team will see the invoice routing and that the supplier is attached to our account? We want to avoid the PO getting stuck because the supplier record is unlinked.
2) For the long term, our IdP team will remap NameID to mail. Could you point them to the exact expected values/format so we don't misconfigure? They asked for a sample SAML assertion format.

If you can confirm (1) and paste a short sample assertion (redacted) for (2) I'll forward to them. Appreciate the quick turnaround and the temporary link.

Best,
